newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan First Int'l to issue US$90m bond.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan First Int'l to issue US$90m bond.

text.p: Taiwan's First International Computer confirmed on Wednesday it would issue US$90 million in convertible bonds to raise funds for overseas purchases and that the issue would likely come before January.
No date for the issue has been announced, but a First International spokeswoman said by telephone it likely would take place before January 1997.
The company said in a statement that it would announce details of the issue at a shareholders' meeting on December 27.
In conjunction with the bond issue, Taiwan's second-largest computer maker plans to raise its total net assets to T$6.6 billion from T$6 billion, the company said in a statement.
The bond issue would save First International about US$37 million in bank interest payments, the statement said.
First International plans to raise its 1996 profit and sales targets in early December, but gave few details.

"Due to the projection that the fourth quarter will see even better earning results, our company has initially decided to announce details of higher earning targets in early December," the statement said.
The company's current 1996 net profit target is T$1.226 billion on sales of T$30 billion.
For the first nine months it posted net profit of T$1.01 billion on sales of T$20.1 billion, compared with profits of T$529 million and sales of $17.39 billion in the 1995 period.
